title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
summary: MessagePack-generated code should be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage so it does not skew coverage results. The thread includes a coverage-tool workaround and a proposed template-based implementation, but no maintainer decision on those proposals.

criteria.text: All MessagePack-generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage.
Users can obtain the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage decoration without being required to configure a new setting; an optional setting is permissible but not required.

open_questions: Should the implementation follow armadavalor's proposal to add the fully qualified attribute to the formatter, string-key formatter, enum/union formatter, and resolver templates and update the verified snapshots, or should users instead be directed to coverage-tool configuration such as b-kurczynski-dl's dotnet-coverage exclusion?
Should generated types also receive GeneratedCode("MessagePack.SourceGenerator", <version>), as armadavalor suggested?
Should the attribute always be emitted, or should an optional setting control it?

thread.title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
thread.author: SergeyBarskiyTyler
thread.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

comments.author: b-kurczynski-dl
comments.body:
Hi Sergey,

I found your ticket as probably I faced the same issue you did. If you use dotnet-coverage to collect the coverage you might adjust your [settings XML](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/additional-tools/dotnet-coverage#settings). I applied the following change and MessagePack's generated classes stopped to be counted:

```
<Configuration>
    <CodeCoverage>
        <Sources>
            <Exclude>
                <Source>obj\\.*\.g\.cs$</Source>
            </Exclude>
        </Sources>
    </CodeCoverage>
</Configuration>
```

Maybe it helps you too.
